clue.text: Safe to criticise one who never grew up

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe, as cracked by a safebreaker
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: A warning that it is safe to find fault with someone who stayed childish.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER, slang for a safe, comes first, then PAN, as in critics panning a play.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's boy hero famously refuses to grow up, so his name stands for any perpetual child.

clue.text: Greek-Cypriot union is one's design

indicators.note: to design is to arrange or form something, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored: I, S, O, N, E, S

explanation.surface: Someone claims a union of Greek Cypriots as their own plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' looks like a noun ending the sentence, but it signals rearranging the six letters of IS ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical movement for Cyprus to join with Greece is known by this Greek term for unification.

clue.text: Examining some money in great detail

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a run of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: Looking closely at a sum of cash, down to the finest particulars.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across monEY IN Great.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it carefully, so the present participle matches examining.

clue.text: Friend to attempt maths problem? It doesn't come to much

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to try is to attempt
a sum is a simple arithmetic problem set in school

explanation.surface: A friend has a go at an arithmetic problem, which proves of little value.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifling amount of money is a small total that adds up to very little; the definition plays on 'come to' as in totalling.

clue.text: United Nations comes up with patent source of energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: patent in the sense of obvious means clear

explanation.surface: The UN arrives with a patented new way of generating power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' suggests an invention, but here it is the adjective meaning plain or evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic fission power is commonly called nuclear, used loosely as a noun for that energy source.

clue.text: Peruvians head east as a precaution

parts.note: the Incas were the ancient people of Peru
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Peruvian travellers set off eastwards, just to be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a link meaning go towards, putting INCAS before E.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase meaning as a safeguard against something happening is equivalent to doing it as a precaution.

clue.text: Victor, out West, is a pretty good shot

indicators.note: out here means the letter for West is taken away

parts.note: a victor is a winner
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A champion, having left the west, is quite an accurate marksman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a name; it is a winner, which loses its W.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery and shooting the ring next to the bull is called the inner, so hitting it is a fairly good shot.

clue.text: A case of building up ready for the maiden flight

definitions.text: A case of building up ready for the maiden flight

parts.words: A case of building up ready for the maiden flight
parts.note: reads like an aircraft being assembled for its first flight, but describes the pupal casing in which a butterfly develops before it first flies

explanation.surface: An aircraft is being assembled ready for its first ever trip into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa's hard protective sheath is where an insect builds its adult form before flying for the first time.

clue.text: Cutting off the lady on a telephone call

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a lady
a ring is a phone call, as in give me a ring

explanation.surface: A woman cuts off a phone conversation midway.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearing is clipping or cutting away, as wool is cut off a sheep.

clue.text: John, half-gone on the bottle, is jolly

indicators.note: half the name has gone, so only its first half remains

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: John, half-cut on drink, is in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-gone on the bottle' suggests drunkenness; it means half of JOHN, then 'on' links VIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone jovial is cheerful and good-humoured, which is what jolly means.

clue.text: Is able to sign for Norwich City FC

parts.note: can means is able to
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone has the ability to sign for a particular English football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' suggests a player's contract; it is the zodiac sign. Norwich City is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich City football club is nicknamed after the yellow songbirds on its badge.

clue.text: Heather Lake's underwear

parts.note: ling is a common name for heather
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather Lake owns some undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather Lake' reads as a person's name; it is two pieces, a plant and a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underclothing in general is known by this French-derived term.

clue.text: At holiday times it may be busy or in repose

definitions.text: At holiday times it may be busy

indicators.note: in means the word or is placed inside the word for repose

parts.note: repose means rest

explanation.surface: At holiday times a place may be bustling or calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy or in repose' looks like a pair of opposites; 'or' is fodder placed in REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside or holiday destination is crowded at peak times, a cryptic description of a holiday town.

clue.text: Abandon Britain, say, to live in isolation here?

parts.note: to desert is to abandon
Britain is an example of an island

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of leaving Britain behind to live a solitary life.
explanation.definitionFit: An uninhabited isle is where a castaway lives alone, cut off from the world.

clue.text: Doctor agonised over second opinions

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician agonised over getting a second medical opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the physician; it is a verb meaning tamper, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical findings about what is wrong with a patient are a doctor's considered judgements.

clue.text: One caring terribly about lack of knowledge

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone frets dreadfully about being uninformed.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of not knowing something is the plain meaning of this noun.

clue.text: Barrister who has joined the family after the match?

definitions.text: Barrister who has joined the family after the match?

parts.words: Barrister who has joined the family after the match
parts.note: a barrister is a man of the law, and the match is a wedding, so this is a daughter's husband

explanation.surface: A lawyer has become part of a family following a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport but means a marriage; a barrister is a son of the law, punningly.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter's husband joins her family by marriage and is called a relation by law.

clue.text: Is role an army at sea? Yes

definitions.text: Is role an army at sea? Yes

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A question whether a naval fighting force counts as an army, answered yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's amphibious infantry corps is a soldierly force serving at sea, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Edited version of the Bible

definitions.meaning: the ... Version is an English translation of the Bible from the 1880s

explanation.definitionFit: Edited text has been amended, and the Bible translation of 1881-85 is named for being an amended King James.

clue.text: Article getting serious towards the end

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
stern means serious or severe

explanation.surface: A piece of writing becomes grave as it nears its conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards the end' means towards the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, moving to the rear is going aft, towards the stern end.

clue.text: Illegally take trick, all the tricks

parts.note: to kid is to fool or trick
in the card game nap, a bid of nap means taking all five tricks

explanation.surface: Someone illegally snatches a card trick and then every other trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap is a card game where calling nap is a bid to win all five tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap is to seize and carry off a person unlawfully.

clue.text: Breaks up the band

definitions.meaning: the band's music is divided into the separate ... each player reads

explanation.definitionFit: To divide is to break up, and the band's music is split into individual instrumental scores.

clue.text: Ivor's out to become a skilled performer

indicators.note: the letters are made to become something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Ivor has gone off to train as an accomplished musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'to become' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a musician or artist of outstanding technical skill.

clue.text: At university, object to tip

parts.note: being up means in residence at university
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A student at college objects to giving a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' and 'tip' look like protest and gratuity; they are aim and overturn. Being UP is British for being at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something upside down or onto its end is to tip it over.

clue.text: Factory shutdowns designed to cure loss

indicators.note: designed means fashioned into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Closing factories is a policy designed to stop losses.
explanation.definitionFit: The shutting down of factories for good is a set of plant closings.

clue.text: Study about river, backing required

indicators.note: backing means the assembled letters are read in reverse
about means the word for study goes around the river

parts.note: a den is a private study
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Investigate the river carefully, as support is necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole container round; 'Study' looks like a verb but is a noun, a private room.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needed is necessary, which is what required means.

clue.text: Fiddles for dances

definitions.meaning: swindles or cheats, as in a fiddle

explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a fiddle or twist, and the twist is a rock-and-roll era dance.

clue.text: Not looking forward to daughter going to university

parts.note: Reading is an English university town

explanation.surface: A father dreads his daughter leaving home for college.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a university in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to anticipate it with fear rather than look forward to it.
